q: Complete the start of David's famous psalm: “The LORD is my…”
why: God cares for His people like a shepherd.
quote: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.

q: In David's shepherd psalm, where does the LORD make him lie down?
why: The Shepherd gives rest.
quote: He makes me lie down in green pastures

q: In David's shepherd psalm, beside what does the LORD lead him?
why: The Shepherd leads to peaceful places.
quote: He leads me beside quiet waters.

q: In David's shepherd psalm, what does the LORD restore?
why: God refreshes us from the inside.
quote: He restores my soul

q: In David's shepherd psalm, why does he fear no evil in the dark valley?
why: God's presence takes away fear.
quote: I will fear no evil, for You are with me

q: In David's shepherd psalm, which two things comfort him?
why: A shepherd uses them to guide and protect.
quote: Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me.

q: In David's shepherd psalm, what will follow him all the days of his life?
why: He will dwell in the house of the LORD forever.
quote: Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life

q: In David's shepherd psalm, what happens to his cup?
why: God blesses him more than enough.
quote: my cup overflows.

q: In the very first psalm, what does the blessed man delight in?
why: He loves God's word.
quote: But his delight is in the Law of the LORD

q: In the very first psalm, when does the blessed man meditate on God's law?
why: God's word fills his thoughts.
quote: and on His law he meditates day and night.

q: In the very first psalm, the blessed man is like what?
why: He grows strong and bears fruit.
quote: He is like a tree planted by streams of water

q: In the very first psalm, what are the wicked like?
why: They have nothing that lasts.
quote: For they are like chaff driven off by the wind.

q: In the very first psalm, the blessed man does not sit in the seat of whom?
why: He avoids the company of scoffers.
quote: or sit in the seat of mockers.

q: In the very first psalm, what does the LORD guard?
why: The way of the wicked will perish.
quote: For the LORD guards the path of the righteous

q: In the very first psalm, what happens to the leaf of the tree by the streams?
why: The blessed man prospers in all he does.
quote: whose leaf does not wither

q: In the longest psalm, God's word is called a lamp to what?
why: God's word shows us where to step.
quote: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.

q: In the longest psalm, God's word is called a light to what?
why: It guides the whole way ahead.
quote: a light to my path.

q: In the longest psalm, where did the writer hide God's word?
why: Knowing God's word helps us resist sin.
quote: I have hidden Your word in my heart that I might not sin against You.

q: In the longest psalm, how can a young person keep his way pure?
a: By guarding it with God's word
why: God's word keeps young people on the right path.
quote: How can a young man keep his way pure? By guarding it according to Your word.

q: In the longest psalm, God's words taste sweeter than what?
why: The writer loved God's words.
quote: sweeter than honey in my mouth!

q: In the longest psalm, why did the writer hide God's word in his heart?
why: God's word protects us from sin.
quote: that I might not sin against You.

q: In a psalm of David, what do the heavens declare?
why: Creation shows how great God is.
quote: The heavens declare the glory of God

q: In a psalm of David, what do his enemies do to get his clothing?
why: The Gospels saw this happen at Jesus' cross.
quote: They divide my garments among them and cast lots for my clothing.

q: In a psalm of David, the LORD is called his light and his what?
why: So David asks, whom shall I fear?
quote: The LORD is my light and my salvation

q: A psalm invites us to taste and see what?
why: Blessed is the one who takes refuge in Him.
quote: Taste and see that the LORD is good

q: A psalm says if you delight yourself in the LORD, He will give you what?
why: Delighting in God shapes what we desire.
quote: Delight yourself in the LORD, and He will give you the desires of your heart.

q: A psalm says the soul longs for God as a deer pants for what?
why: The writer thirsts for God.
quote: As the deer pants for streams of water

q: A psalm calls God our refuge and what?
why: He is an ever-present help in trouble.
quote: God is our refuge and strength

q: In a psalm, what does God tell us to be, so we know that He is God?
why: God will be exalted among the nations.
quote: Be still and know that I am God

q: In David's psalm of repentance, what does he ask God to create in him?
why: David wanted to be made right with God.
quote: Create in me a clean heart, O God

q: A psalm of thanksgiving tells all the earth to make what to the LORD?
why: Worship can be loud and glad.
quote: Make a joyful noise to the LORD, all the earth.

q: A psalm of thanksgiving says we are God's people and the sheep of what?
why: God made us and we belong to Him.
quote: we are His people, and the sheep of His pasture.

q: A psalm of thanksgiving says to enter God's gates with what?
why: And His courts with praise.
quote: Enter His gates with thanksgiving and His courts with praise

q: A psalm says God removes our sins from us as far as what?
a: The east is from the west
wrong: The sky is from the sea
why: God's forgiveness is complete.
quote: As far as the east is from the west, so far has He removed our transgressions from us.

q: A psalm says: This is the day that the LORD has made; we will do what?
a: Rejoice and be glad in it
why: Every day is a gift from God.
quote: This is the day that the LORD has made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.

q: In a song of ascents, where does the writer say his help comes from?
a: The LORD, Maker of heaven and earth
why: He lifts his eyes beyond the hills to God.
quote: My help comes from the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth.

q: A song of ascents says the Protector of Israel will neither slumber nor what?
why: God never stops watching over His people.
quote: the Protector of Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.

q: In a psalm of David, how does he say he was made?
why: David praised God for how He made him.
quote: for I am fearfully and wonderfully made.

q: The very last psalm calls on everything that has breath to do what?
why: The book of Psalms ends in praise.
quote: Let everything that has breath praise the LORD!

q: A psalm says God will command His angels to do what for you?
a: Guard you in all your ways
why: God protects those who trust Him.
quote: For He will command His angels concerning you to guard you in all your ways.

q: A song of ascents says how good and pleasant it is when brothers do what?
why: Unity among God's people is a blessing.
quote: how good and pleasant it is when brothers live together in harmony!

q: A psalm says the length of our days is seventy years, or how many if we are strong?
why: Life passes quickly.
quote: The length of our days is seventy years— or eighty if we are strong

q: A psalm says that in God's sight a thousand years are like what?
why: God is not limited by time.
quote: For in Your sight a thousand years are but a day that passes

q: In a psalm of the exile, by which rivers did God's people sit and weep?
why: They wept when they remembered Zion.
quote: By the rivers of Babylon we sat and wept when we remembered Zion.

q: In the psalm of the exiles in Babylon, where did they hang their harps?
why: They were too sad to sing.
quote: There on the willows we hung our harps

q: The psalm about a deer panting for water is a Maskil of whom?
why: The sons of Korah wrote several psalms.
quote: A Maskil of the sons of Korah.

q: To which tune was the psalm “My God, my God, why have You forsaken me?” set?
why: It is a psalm of David for the choirmaster.
quote: To the tune of “The Doe of the Dawn.”

q: In a psalm of David, the heavens are called the work of what?
why: David wondered why God cares for people.
quote: When I behold Your heavens, the work of Your fingers

q: In the shortest psalm, who is called to praise the LORD?
why: God's love reaches every people.
quote: Praise the LORD, all you nations!

q: In a psalm of David, where did God knit him together?
why: God formed him before he was born.
quote: You knit me together in my mother’s womb.
